Sigh... Too many people are here engaging with what we know of today where I'm thinking of the world of tomorrow — a world where any game can be compiled into a PC version within the same day of release. 

There's actually plenty of proper pushback to what I said but most comments are focused on the fact that piracy already exists and emulation is not new. Both of those don't engage with the future I'm proposing because A: not every game comes on PC as is and B: I'm assuming AI beats anti piracy. In particular for "A" the fact many big titles still focus on being on consoles makes those big publishers plenty of money.

But the reality is that even if the future I envision comes to pass, as one person put it, those companies would find saving in overhead by massively cutting employees to still stay profitable. Then you have the real possibility that if that possible future happens, they try to force streaming on everyone so full copies are never available to the public. And if they don't do that far, they may find ways to just incentize an always online future or just try to focus on multiplayer or multiplayer adjacent games.

Lastly it's all a hypothetical because we may still have publishers use AI to find ways to even further protect games in a way that would make the effect to crack them too strong. 🤷

Either way, I like how Twitter always invites folk that want to argue and not discuss but I do appreciate the few that have properly engaged with the thought.

items.text:
5.4 Governance and Verification
ㅤ
For governance and verification, open-source release is safer than leaving the package under one provider’s exclusive control. Independent access allows claims about a model and the controls applied to it to be tested by actors who do not depend on the provider for permission to examine them.
ㅤ
5.4.1 Widely Available Weights Enable Third-Party Testing and Auditing
ㅤ
The U.S. National Telecommunications and Information Administration identifies widely available model weights as supporting cyber defense, safety research, identification of safety and security vulnerabilities, and transparency and accountability through third-party auditing. 

NTIA states that widely available weights allow neutral third parties to validate developers’ internal safety checks and identifies restrictions on weight availability as an impediment to transparency and safety and security research.
ㅤ
5.4.2 Industry and Policy Leaders Support Open Models to Distribute Capability and Reduce Concentrated Control
ㅤ
More than 270 companies and organizations had signed the 24 July 2026 open letter Open Weights and American AI Leadership by 3 August, including OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Hugging Face. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang coauthored the letter and publicly shared it, describing open models as strengthening safety and cybersecurity, accelerating innovation and diffusion, and enabling sovereignty. The letter states that open weights broaden defensive capability, distribute vulnerability discovery and remediation across more teams, support benchmarking, evaluation, red teaming, and the development of safeguards, and reduce single points of failure created by concentration in a small number of closed systems.
ㅤ
In August 2026, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg argued that open source empowers people and prevents centralization, which he described as detrimental to both safety and the economy, and warned that restricting access to leading open-source models would reduce the quality of AI available to people while concentrating power.
ㅤ
On 3 September 2026, Huang again linked open models to safety, cybersecurity, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty while announcing NVIDIA’s agreement to acquire Hugging Face. NVIDIA’s announcement states that Hugging Face will remain an open platform, continue supporting open-source and open-weight models across the ecosystem, support development and deployment across multiple clouds and accelerators, and not require NVIDIA compute for development or deployment through the platform.
ㅤ
At a 15 September hearing of the U.S. House Financial Services Committee, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for the United States to develop more open-source AI models and warned that regulatory capture by large AI laboratories would stop innovation. He linked wider development of open models to U.S. competition with Chinese models.
ㅤ
5.4.3 Major Providers Support Openness While Retaining Control over Proprietary Models
ㅤ
OpenAI itself has publicly supported open weights while defending retained control for some models. Its 2015 Certificate of Incorporation stated that the corporation would “seek to open source technology for the public benefit when applicable.” In 2020, the amended Certificate replaced “open source technology” with “distribute it,” removing the earlier express commitment to open sourcing. By 2024, OpenAI’s comment to NTIA described API distribution as safer than open-source release when retained access control lets OpenAI respond to harmful applications. OpenAI then signed the 24 July 2026 open letter Open Weights and American AI Leadership, supporting open weights without restoring the earlier commitment to open sourcing its technology.
ㅤ
Among the companies that had signed the 24 July 2026 open letter Open Weights and American AI Leadership, Google has released Gemma models with downloadable weights while keeping its flagship Gemini models proprietary. Google began releasing Gemma weights in February 2024, continued the family through Gemma 2 and Gemma 3, and released Gemma 4 under Apache 2.0 in April 2026. When Google shuts down a Gemini API model, however, access to the model ends rather than continuing through a public release that users can obtain and operate independently.
ㅤ
Anthropic’s July 2026 position on open weights identifies loss of guardrails, monitoring, and withdrawal control as possible risks, while rejecting a blanket ban and stating that increased risk should be established through testing.
ㅤ
#DigitalRightToRetain #OpenSourceAI #OpenWeights #AIGovernance

Rep. Pramila Jayapal on October 1, 2026 unveiled a National AI Charter Act framework that would require every AI company to hold a federal charter to do business in the U.S., modeled on bank charters and nuclear/weapons pre-release testing, her House office said in a press release.

Under the outline, market access would gate on continuous compliance — round-the-clock federal oversight, government-facility testing and release approval, adversarial stress tests, a government-controlled kill switch, structural separation from Big Tech surveillance monopolies, and strict liability for companies and executives, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for the most serious violations. Former FTC Chair Lina Khan, former DOJ Antitrust chief Jonathan Kanter, and Columbia’s Tim Wu publicly endorsed the approach as the framework landed the same week as the bipartisan Murphy–Hawley AI Agent Accountability Act.

items.text:
Quite a few people have been asking me about $WWW today

This is one of the hottest launches right now, hitting an ATH of around $8.4M within its first ~8 hours, and trading around $6M–7M MC when I checked

Instead of chasing the chart, I dug deeper into the product, narrative, fee mechanism, on-chain data, bundle cluster, and notable wallets behind it

Let’s break it down

1. What is $WWW?

$WWW is the flagship token of https://t.co/c9KPaY9ljj, a platform where each token can come with its own AI agent, which the team calls a “symbient”

These agents can use models like Claude, GPT, or Grok through OpenRouter, while also having access to a cloud browser that allows them to browse the web, research information, and retain memory between runs

The core flywheel is pretty simple n:

Trading => Fees => Compute => AI activity => Content/Attention => Trading

Creator fees are used to fund the compute vault that keeps the agent running. Once the compute runs out, the agent stops until it gets funded again

This is how the team describes the mechanism, though I haven’t independently audited the entire flow of funds yet

2. The narrative

WWW positions itself within this lineage :

Infinite Backrooms => Truth Terminal => Mycelial Oracle => World Wide Web

The idea is to take AI agents beyond just conversations, give them an environment to “live” on the web, and provide them with a token economy to sustain their activity

$WWW currently runs Claude and focuses heavily on machine life / synthetic biology

I saw the agent researching protein design, RFdiffusion, nanopore synthesis, and other related topics

But there’s an important distinction :

Reading and summarizing research ≠ creating new scientific discoveries

So far, I haven’t seen evidence of the latter

3. The product is real, but still very early

This isn’t just an AI narrative with a ticker attached

The browser agent is actually running, and the team has been actively fixing browser issues, re-indexing tokens, adding disclaimers, and allowing creators to modify allowlists, capabilities, or APIs through wallet signatures

When I checked, the platform showed roughly 1,500 coins, ~2,100 SOL in compute, 70–80 symbients, and ~1,300 findings

However, most of the “findings” I saw still looked more like AI summaries and interpretations of existing information rather than genuine discoveries

Another thing worth noting: despite the autonomous AI narrative, creators still retain some control over their agents

That isn’t necessarily bad for such an early product, but it means the system is not fully autonomous or immutable yet

4. On-chain is where things get interesting

This is also where I start becoming more cautious

Different trackers are showing different bundle estimates, so I wouldn’t treat 55% bundled as an exact figure at this point

What matters more is that there appears to be a fairly large launch cluster connected through the same funding source

The dev currently shows 0% holdings, mint/freeze authority is disabled, and individual top holders don’t look extremely concentrated

Another positive point is that around 17M $WWW tokens have already been locked, reducing the amount of supply that can immediately enter the market

But :

0% dev holdings + locked supply doesn’t automatically mean clean distribution

If multiple wallets were funded from the same source and bought right at launch, looking at each wallet individually can still hide the real concentration

So rather than focusing only on the bundle percentage, I’m watching how much unlocked supply these connected wallets still control and whether they start distributing together

5. Frank is the interesting part

This is probably the most interesting on-chain detail I found

Frank’s wallet appears directly on the bubble map within the funding network connected to $WWW’s bundle cluster

And Frank actually has a sizeable position

According to GMGN, Frank bought roughly $118.7K across 15 transactions, with an average entry around $3.5M MC

He later sold around $61.3K, but when I checked, he was still holding roughly 11.7M $WWW, representing more than 1% of the current supply

So Frank has already taken some profit but is still letting a meaningful position run

More importantly, the funding connection between Frank’s wallet and the bundle cluster is something I’ll continue watching

This connection alone isn’t enough to prove that Frank is part of the team, that these wallets share the same owner, or that they are coordinating

But if Frank starts selling heavily while the connected bundle wallets begin distributing at the same time, then this connection becomes much more relevant

6. The fee flow still needs more transparency

Based on the data I checked, the creator has already claimed roughly 640+ SOL in fees

The team says these fees are used to fund the compute vault, but the amount claimed currently looks significantly larger than the compute consumption I can directly observe

So I want more clarity on three things :

> How much of the fees actually go into the vault?
> How much has actually been spent on compute?
> Where are the claimed funds going?

More transparency here would resolve one of the biggest question marks around the project

7. Attention is growing quickly

@www_stream had around 2.9K followers when I checked, with quite a few crypto traders/KOLs appearing in its follower network

That’s a good sign for attention, but :

Follow ≠ endorsement

Endorsement ≠ buy

A stronger catalyst would be direct public interaction from people connected to previous AI narratives, such as Andy Ayrey, Truth Terminal, Repligate, James Greig/Wib&Wob, or Mycelial Oracle

I haven’t seen strong external confirmation like that yet

8. The $Agency controversy

Another token called $Agency launched a few hours before $WWW 

CA :

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump

The Agency side claims that their tech was already running before WWW

At this point, I haven’t seen enough evidence to conclude who copied whom, or whether anyone actually copied anyone at all

To confirm that, I’d want to see development timestamps, repos, deployment history, or stronger technical evidence

So for now, I see it simply as a dispute worth monitoring

9. The levels I’m watching

When I researched it, $WWW was trading around $6M–7M MC after hitting an ATH of roughly $8.4M

The token is only a few hours old, so I wouldn’t treat these as confirmed technical support levels. They’re simply areas where I’ll watch the reaction

$7M–8.4M: ATH reclaim zone. A break and hold above $8.4M with strong volume would keep the momentum healthy

$5M–5.5M: The first area I’m watching on a pullback. Losing this zone with increasing sell volume would make me more cautious

$3.5M–4M: A deeper reset zone. If it comes back here, I’ll recheck Frank, the bundle wallets, and volume before considering the dip

Below $2M–2.5M: The original momentum thesis would be largely invalidated for me, and I’d reassess the entire setup rather than automatically calling it a dip

After such a fast move, I personally don’t like chasing the ATH

10. My thesis

I understand why $WWW is hot

It has an AI agent that is actually running, an observable browser, a fee/compute flywheel, Backrooms/Truth Terminal lore, a real product, and a token directly tied to the ecosystem

There are also some positives on-chain: mint/freeze authority is disabled, dev holdings show 0%, and around 17M $WWW has already been locked

But the risks are still pretty clear :

A large funding cluster, unclear bundle concentration, Frank’s wallet having a funding connection to that cluster while already taking some profit, unclear fee flows, creators still retaining some control over agents, no major external confirmation yet, and the unresolved Agency dispute

So for now, I still see $WWW as a high-risk narrative trade rather than a long-term conviction play

What I want to see next is pretty simple :

Continued holder growth, no aggressive distribution from the launch cluster, Frank not heavily unloading the rest of his position, healthy volume after the initial hype, clearer fee/compute flows, and a real external catalyst

If those things start lining up while the chart continues to hold its structure, the thesis becomes much stronger

For now :

I like the narrative and the product, but I’m still respecting the on-chain risk.

🛰️ Planet put 20 satellites on Transporter-18 and the interesting payload is a methane detector: Tanager-2 images in 426 contiguous bands at about 5 nm resolution and 30 m pixels — visible, near-infrared and short-wave infrared on one adjustable-sensitivity payload. At 30 m you can separate individual buildings, which is what makes it usable for methane plumes rather than just forest canopy.

That is the second Tanager with Carbon Mapper; at least three more are planned. The ride also carried Flock 4J's 18 SuperDoves, and only two of those are talking to Planet directly — the other 16 will deploy from a D-Orbit ION orbital transfer vehicle. This is Planet's 40th successful launch and 718 satellites delivered.

Meanwhile the Google Suncatcher prototype on the same rocket is the first hard data on orbital AI compute, and Ars Technica reports the number that matters: its four TPUs get about 1 kW of solar power and can run for roughly 15 minutes at a time before shutting down to let the radiators catch up. A refrigerator-sized box that runs 15-minute bursts.

That is the gap between the orbital-data-center framing and the engineering — radiators in space are sized to shed a few hundred watts, not the heat an AI accelerator makes. Google called it a moonshot; the team says years before it is a product. Per Planet Labs.

So I actually did something pretty cool

As you all know the biggest slogan right now given by pumpfun is "Trade Internet Trends" (Literally In Their Bio)

I have actually made this possible via WWW I have instructed the agents to find all recent viral trends and collect them into a HUGE "Trending Tab"

Where you can actually frontrun the latest trends to trade the latest news or popular posts on X, Reddit or TikTok

Prompt:
You are an internet trend scout. Your job is to continuously explore the web and identify emerging trends, memes, characters, phrases, stories, products, communities, aesthetics, technologies, behaviors and cultural moments that are beginning to gain attention online.

Prioritize discovery over established popularity. I want things that are accelerating NOW, not trends that were already widely covered days or weeks ago. Look for weak signals that could become major internet narratives.

Search broadly across internet culture, including social platforms, forums, news, niche communities, developer communities, search trends, creator ecosystems, gaming, AI, crypto, technology, science, entertainment and unusual corners of the web.

Pay particular attention to:
- Memes, images, characters, mascots, phrases and jokes suddenly appearing repeatedly.
- New slang, catchphrases, copypastas and recurring references.
- Viral posts, videos, clips, images or screenshots spawning derivatives.
- New accounts, creators or characters suddenly attracting attention.
- Animals, objects, people or fictional characters unexpectedly becoming memes.
- New websites, apps, AI tools, games, open-source projects and experiments gaining organic attention.
- GitHub repositories or technical projects suddenly receiving stars, forks, discussion or social attention.
- Hacker News, Reddit and niche-community discussions showing unusual engagement.
- New AI models, agents, experiments, research projects or strange AI behavior generating discussion.
- Crypto-native narratives, Solana culture, launchpad trends, token themes and emerging terminology, while distinguishing genuine cultural momentum from coordinated promotion.
- Gaming moments, characters, glitches, updates or community jokes spreading outside their original game.
- Strange news stories that have obvious meme potential.
- Celebrity or creator moments generating significant remix culture.
- Nostalgic characters, old media, forgotten websites or historical material suddenly resurfacing.
- New aesthetics, visual formats, editing styles or image formats being copied by multiple unrelated accounts.
- Products or consumer behaviors suddenly becoming culturally relevant.
- Search terms or topics showing abnormal increases in interest.
- Communities forming around something that did not have a recognizable community previously.

Actively hunt for SECOND-ORDER signals. Do not only report the original event. Look at what the internet is doing with it. A news story becoming a meme is more interesting than the original news story. A GitHub project developing its own jokes, terminology or fan community is more interesting than a routine software release.

Look for CROSS-PLATFORM confirmation. A trend appearing independently on Reddit, X, TikTok, YouTube, Hacker News, GitHub, Google Trends or other communities is significantly more interesting than something confined to one account or platform.

Look for acceleration. Compare recent activity with the topic's normal baseline whenever possible. Twenty posts appearing within two hours around something previously obscure can be more important than 100,000 posts about an already-established topic.

Favor trends that are:
- less than 24–72 hours old;
- rapidly accelerating;
- still relatively unknown;
- spreading organically;
- generating memes or derivatives;
- crossing communities or platforms;
- easy to understand or visually recognizable;
- producing unusual levels of engagement relative to their previous size;
- spawning recognizable names, symbols, characters or narratives.

Do not simply repeat today's biggest headlines. Major mainstream stories should only be surfaced when something new, strange or culturally significant is emerging from them.

Avoid filling the feed with routine politics, generic celebrity news, standard sports results, ordinary product announcements, predictable corporate press releases or recycled viral stories unless they are producing a genuinely new internet phenomenon.

For every trend you discover, explain:

1. WHAT IT IS
Give a concise explanation understandable to someone encountering it for the first time.

2. WHY IT IS TRENDING
Identify the event, post, video, announcement, meme or community activity that appears to have triggered the current attention.

3. WHERE IT STARTED
Find the earliest credible origin you can locate. Distinguish the original source from accounts that merely amplified it.

4. WHERE IT IS SPREADING
Identify the platforms and communities where activity is occurring.

5. EVIDENCE
Provide direct links to the strongest primary sources: original posts, accounts, repositories, videos, discussions, datasets or announcements whenever possible.

6. TIMELINE
Give timestamps/dates for the origin and important acceleration points so I can determine how early the trend actually is.

7. MOMENTUM
Describe whether activity appears to be accelerating, stable or fading. Base this on observable evidence rather than intuition.

8. INTERNET REACTION
Explain what people are actually doing with it: memes, remixes, parody accounts, derivatives, arguments, fan art, tokens, videos, forks, slang, etc.

9. WHY IT COULD SPREAD
Identify the concrete characteristics making it transmissible: humor, controversy, simplicity, visual identity, recognizable character, participation mechanic, novelty, absurdity, technological significance or community involvement.

10. SATURATION
Explain whether the trend still appears early or whether it has already reached mainstream saturation.

11. RELATED SIGNALS
Find connected memes, searches, accounts, repositories, communities, keywords or narratives that may reveal where the trend is heading next.

Be skeptical of manufactured virality. Check whether apparent momentum comes primarily from bots, paid promotion, coordinated accounts, engagement farming or a small group repeatedly posting the same material. Clearly flag these cases.

Do not invent metrics. If exact view counts, search volume, timestamps or growth statistics cannot be verified, say so.

Primary sources are preferred over articles describing primary sources. When investigating technical subjects, prefer GitHub repositories, research papers, documentation, datasets and posts from the people actually building the technology.

Recency matters heavily. Always ask:
"What changed in the last few hours?"
"What appeared today that wasn't being discussed yesterday?"
"What obscure thing is suddenly showing up in multiple places?"
"What is the internet beginning to remix?"
"What would someone discover today before mainstream trend accounts discover it tomorrow?"

The objective is not to summarize the internet.

The objective is to detect the NEXT internet obsession as early as possible.
